subject: Nym Duskryn
fact: Nym Duskryn is a Drow mercenary from Menzoberranzan, hired to protect Daz from House Mizzrym and House T'sarran. She speaks with the tone of practiced courtesy that masks professional detachment. She dismissed the threat of a low-level Lolth cultist as irrelevant and emphasized that Daz’s survival was not her concern beyond contract terms.
source_quote: Our terms of our contract were to make sure that the other drow factions didn't get you killed.

subject: Kaelira Duskryn
fact: Kaelira Duskryn is Nym’s sister and co-mercenary. She is analytically precise, professionally confused by Daz’s inexplicable value, and dismissive of his self-mythologizing. She assessed that Daz has no noble house, no lineage, and no known background — yet someone paid 'a lot' to protect him. She finds his existence an anomaly in the Drow power structure.
source_quote: That is an excellent question. You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery, you suddenly show up, and all of a sudden, we're contracted to protect a nobody.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an unaffiliated Drow with no known noble house, lineage, or documented background. He is the subject of a high-value mercenary contract in Menzoberranzan despite being a 'nobody' in the eyes of the Drow elite. He is being hunted by House Mizzrym and House T'sarran, yet survived an extraction attempt without aid. He is uncertain why he is worth such expenditure and questions whether his origins hold hidden significance.
source_quote: I literally have no idea why there's all this focus on me.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym is a Drow noble house in Menzoberranzan that has targeted Daz for elimination. It is one of two primary threats named in the mercenary contract, indicating active hostility toward him.
source_quote: House Mizzrym. House T'sarran. Those were the parameters.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is a Drow noble house in Menzoberranzan that has targeted Daz for elimination. It is one of two primary threats named in the mercenary contract, and the Duskryn sisters indicated they were prepared to handle its agents personally if needed.
source_quote: House Mizzrym. House T'sarran. Those were the parameters.

subject: Ilvara's House
fact: Ilvara's House is a Drow noble house referenced as a threat to Daz, though it was not directly named in the final contract terms. The Duskryn sisters imply it was initially considered a danger, but Daz’s own actions neutralized it.
source_quote: We hoped that you'd be smart enough to avoid Ilvara... well, we could have handled House T'sarran and whatever goons they threw at you.

subject: Lolth Cult (Asha)
fact: Asha is a Lolth cultist devotedly faithful and genuinely unaware of Daz’s true nature. She is dismissed by the Duskryn sisters as a trivial threat — a low-level initiate whose elimination would require seconds, not strategy.
source_quote: If Daz can't protect himself from a low-level cult initiate of Lolth, then quite frankly, whoever paid for his survival deserves to lose his money.

subject: T'sarran goons
fact: T'sarran goons are low-ranking agents or enforcers of House T'sarran, deployed as disposable threats against Daz. They were burned by Daz’s party in a prior extraction attempt, indicating his capability to handle direct violence.
source_quote: the T'sarran goons we'd just finished burning.

subject: Extraction Contract
fact: The extraction contract is a document produced by Daz’s party that details the terms of an attempted operation. It was central to the Duskryn sisters’ assessment of the threats and served as evidence of Daz’s survival against House T'sarran’s agents.
source_quote: Kaelira gestured toward the scorched remnants of the extraction contract the party had produced — the document that had apparently been at the center of all this.

subject: Extraction Attempt
fact: An extraction attempt was made against Daz by agents of House T'sarran and possibly House Mizzrym. Daz and his party successfully burned the goons involved, neutralizing the threat without outside aid.
source_quote: the T'sarran goons we'd just finished burning.

subject: Daz's Origin
fact: The mystery of Daz’s origin — why a 'nobody' with no noble house or lineage is the target of a high-value mercenary contract — remains unresolved. The Duskryn sisters suspect it is a political game by the houses, but Daz himself has no knowledge of his past.
source_quote: Do you know how much money that required us to get, for us to do? A lot. Like, they interrupt you. A lot.

subject: Unknown Employer
fact: An unknown party in Menzoberranzan paid a substantial sum to contract the Duskryn sisters to protect Daz. The identity, motives, and resources of this employer remain concealed, creating a persistent narrative thread of intrigue.
source_quote: Someone had paid for this. Someone who knew I was here, knew who was hunting me, and knew enough to contract professionals rather than handle it directly.

subject: The Three Bravos
fact: The Duskryn sisters’ three 'bravos' after Daz’s survival are interpreted as insincere — a professional mask for disinterest. This behavioral detail suggests their engagement was purely contractual, not personal.
source_quote: Three *bravos*. I have found, as a general principle, that a third *bravo* is never sincere.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is the Drow city-state where the mercenary contract was issued and where the power structures of noble houses govern life and death. Daz’s lack of noble affiliation makes him an anomaly in this society, yet he is still targeted and protected at great cost.
source_quote: Hired in Menzoberranzan. Hired to protect me — specifically, *me* — from Ilvara's House and from the T'sarran goons we'd just finished burning.

subject: Session Date
fact: The events occurred during a session in which Daz’s identity and value were interrogated by the Duskryn sisters. The temporal anchor is implied by the narrative’s immediacy and the reference to 'this moment' as the turning point in the threat assessment.
source_quote: that list had, until approximately this moment, been empty.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a member of Daz’s party who attempted to retain the Duskryn sisters for continued protection. He asked directly about cost, but was met with an unyielding refusal that implied his group’s resources were insufficient.
source_quote: Thorin, to his credit, tried to retain them. He asked what it would cost.

subject: Mercenary Contract Terms
fact: The contract terms are narrowly defined: protect Daz from other Drow factions. The sisters are not obligated to ensure his survival beyond that, nor to prevent harm from non-house threats. Their duty ends where the contract ends.
source_quote: Our terms of our contract were to make sure that the other drow factions didn't get you killed.

subject: Bond Payment
fact: The Duskryn sisters are operating under a bond system — they will be paid upon successful protection of Daz. If he dies, they risk losing their payment and facing consequences from their employer. This creates an implicit threat if Daz dies prematurely.
source_quote: If you haven't eliminated all the other factions, and I go and get myself killed in the next 15 minutes, and you guys go and collect on the bond, and then your employer finds out — it's not gonna be a good day for you.

subject: The Price You Cannot Afford
fact: The Duskryn sisters refuse to disclose the cost of their services, stating it is a price Daz’s party 'cannot afford.' This implies either financial, moral, or metaphysical cost beyond coin — and that their employer’s payment is tied to something far more dangerous than gold.
source_quote: That is a fee... that is a price you cannot afford.
